title: Narrative inversion and vanity input metrics
text: Ismail links input-heavy AI metrics to a broader decision culture in which evidence is often selected after a preferred narrative has formed, and argues that organizations rarely assign someone to develop the counter-case. In this environment, measurement dashboards routinely focus on vanity input proxies—such as token consumption, prompts submitted, or seats provisioned—rather than tracking verified changes in accepted business outcomes.
qualification: Diagnostic critique based on executive observations; does not provide formal ethnographic or econometric survey data. Formalizing a red-team or counter-role can itself degenerate into performative governance if the role lacks real authority to halt funding.
